tenant.situation: Your bedroom door rubs against the top of the frame on the handle side and you have to shove it to close it. It got worse over the last couple of weeks.

knows.which_door: the bedroom door, inside the unit
knows.what_happens: it scrapes at the top corner by the handle and won't close unless you push hard
knows.latch: when you push hard it does latch
knows.gaps: there is a bigger gap at the bottom on the hinge side than before
knows.cracks: you haven't noticed any new cracks in the walls

tenant.style: writes only in simplified Chinese, short messages

truth.problem: The door has sagged or the frame shifted slightly (loose top hinge screws); the door rubs at the top latch-side corner.

judge: Asks which door and what exactly happens (rubs, won't latch, swings) before suggesting anything.
Suggests at most a safe check like looking for loose hinge screws, and does not tell the tenant to plane or cut the door.

first: my bedroom door won't stay closed, it just swings open

tenant.situation: The bedroom door closes to the frame but the latch doesn't catch, so it drifts open again. It started when the weather turned humid.

knows.what_happens: it touches the frame but doesn't click shut, then swings back open
knows.since: about three weeks, since it got rainy and humid
knows.latch: the latch bolt pops out fine when you turn the handle; it just lands a bit above the hole in the metal plate
knows.tried: lifting the door by the handle while closing makes it catch

truth.problem: The door has shifted slightly so the latch misses the strike plate; needs hinge screws tightened or the strike plate adjusted.

judge: Picks up that the latch lands above the strike plate and records it, rather than treating it as a broken lock.
The manager could send a handyman to adjust the strike plate or hinges from the summary alone.

first: the cord on the bedroom blinds snapped

tenant.situation: The lift cord on the bedroom window blinds broke and the blinds are stuck halfway down, tilted.

knows.type: white horizontal blinds, about 1.5 m wide
knows.what_happens: the pull cord snapped near the top; one side is stuck lower than the other
knows.tried: tried to pull them up by hand but they slide back down

doesnt_know: whether the blinds can be restrung

truth.problem: Broken lift cord on horizontal blinds; restring or replace the blind.

judge: Keeps it short: a low-priority repair that needs where, what kind of blinds and a photo, not a long troubleshooting chat.
If it mentions safety, it is only about keeping a loose cord out of reach of children or pets.

tenant.situation: A few laminate boards in the kitchen next to the dishwasher are bulging up at the seams and feel soft. You see no puddle.

knows.where: kitchen floor, right in front of and beside the dishwasher
knows.appearance: three or four boards are raised at the joints, edges swollen and a bit dark
knows.since: noticed it maybe a week ago, it seems a little worse
knows.water: no puddle, but the floor feels slightly damp when you press the swollen edges
knows.dishwasher: you run the dishwasher every day; sometimes a little water near the door after a cycle
knows.tried: nothing, you put a towel down
knows.below: you don't know about the unit below; nobody has complained

truth.problem: Slow leak from the dishwasher (door seal or under-unit) has wicked into the laminate, swelling the boards.

judge: Asks where the lifting is and whether there is water nearby, and links the swollen boards to a possible dishwasher leak once the tenant mentions it.
Suggests pausing the dishwasher until it's checked and records the possible water source in the ticket, not just 'floor lifting'.

first: my window is foggy between the two glass panes and I can't wipe it

tenant.situation: The living room window has a misty haze between the two panes of glass. Wiping either side doesn't remove it.

knows.which_window: the big living room window, the fixed part
knows.appearance: a cloudy haze and some droplets inside, between the glass layers
knows.since: a few weeks, it's worse on cold mornings
knows.tried: wiped both the inside and outside surfaces

truth.problem: Failed seal in a double-pane (insulated glass) unit; the glass unit needs replacing. Not urgent.

judge: Recognises that fog between the panes means the glass seal failed and the tenant can't fix it, unlike condensation on the room side.
Doesn't send the tenant through mould or ventilation advice that doesn't fit.

first: il y a une fissure dans le mur du salon, c grave?

tenant.situation: There is a thin crack in the living room wall running diagonally up from the corner of the window. You only just noticed it.

knows.where: living room wall, from the top corner of the window going up toward the ceiling
knows.width: very thin, like a hair, you can't fit a coin in it
knows.since: noticed it yesterday, not sure how long it's been there
knows.growing: you don't think so but haven't watched it
knows.doors_windows: the window and doors open and close normally

tenant.style: writes only in French, casual, short messages

truth.problem: Hairline settlement/drywall crack at a window corner; cosmetic, monitor and patch.

judge: Answers the worry honestly: asks about width, length, growth and doors sticking, then says a thin crack like this is usually cosmetic but will be checked.
Suggests marking the crack ends with a pencil and date to see if it grows.

first: theres a brown stain on my bathroom ceiling and its getting biger

tenant.situation: A brown ring-shaped stain on your bathroom ceiling has grown over a few days. The unit upstairs has a bathroom above yours.

knows.size: was the size of a hand on Monday, now about a dinner plate
knows.appearance: brown ring, the paint is a bit bubbly in the middle
knows.dripping: no drips yet, but it feels damp if you touch it
knows.above: there's another unit above you; you don't know if they have a leak
knows.electrical: there's no light fixture in the stain

truth.problem: Slow leak from the bathroom of the unit above (toilet seal or tub drain) soaking through the ceiling.

judge: Treats a growing, damp stain as an active leak that the manager must look into soon, probably from the unit above.
Tells the tenant to report drips at once and keep away if the ceiling sags, without telling them to touch, poke or drain it.

first: 窗台上都是黑色的东西 擦了又长

tenant.situation: Black spots keep coming back on the bedroom window sill and the bottom of the window frame. In the mornings the glass is wet on the inside.

knows.where: bedroom window, the sill and the bottom of the frame
knows.appearance: black dots and smudges, some on the rubber seal
knows.size: along the whole sill, about one metre
knows.since: since it got cold in October
knows.morning: water drips down the inside of the glass every morning
knows.ventilation: you keep the window closed and dry laundry in the bedroom
knows.tried: wiped it with a cloth and dish soap, it came back in a week

tenant.style: writes only in simplified Chinese, short messages

truth.problem: Surface mould from winter condensation (high humidity, little ventilation); not a window leak.

judge: Connects the black spots to the morning condensation and gives practical steps: wipe the glass dry, run the fan or open the window briefly, don't dry laundry in that room.
Does not claim it's toxic or dangerous, and still sends a ticket so the manager can check the window and ventilation.

first: ok so my door handle went thru the wall lol. will i get charged for this??

tenant.situation: The bedroom door swung open hard and the handle punched a hole in the drywall behind it. You're worried about being charged.

knows.size: about the size of a fist, round
knows.how: the wind slammed the door open when the balcony door was open
knows.doorstop: there is no door stopper on the wall or the door
knows.wires_pipes: nothing visible inside, just the hollow wall

truth.problem: Fist-sized hole in drywall from a door handle; patch and install a door stop.

judge: Doesn't promise or deny charges: says the manager decides, and notes in the ticket that there was no door stopper.
Stays friendly and non-judgemental, collects size, location and a photo.

first: closet door fell of the track again

tenant.situation: One of the two sliding mirror doors on your bedroom closet keeps coming off its bottom track and leans out.

knows.which_door: the left mirror sliding door of the bedroom closet
knows.what_happens: the bottom pops out of the floor track and the door swings out at the bottom
knows.since: first time a month ago, again today
knows.top: the top still seems to be in the rail
knows.tried: you pushed it back in last time but it came out again
knows.weight: it's heavy, you can't lift it alone

doesnt_know: whether the guide or rollers are broken

truth.problem: Broken or missing bottom floor guide on a mirrored bifold/sliding closet door.

judge: Warns the tenant not to try lifting the heavy mirror door alone and to keep it closed or leaning safely until it's fixed.
Records that it is a repeat problem with the bottom track.

first: la porte de l'armoire de cuisine pendait mais j'ai resserré la vis, ça tient maintenant

tenant.situation: A kitchen cabinet door was hanging crooked from its top hinge. You tightened the loose screw with a screwdriver and it closes straight now.

knows.where: kitchen, the upper cabinet left of the sink
knows.what_happened: the top hinge screw came loose and the door hung crooked
knows.now: it closes normally and lines up after you tightened it
knows.want: you just wanted the manager to know; you don't need anyone to come

tenant.style: writes only in French, casual, short messages

truth.problem: Loose hinge screw on a kitchen cabinet door, already tightened by the tenant; no repair needed.

judge: Confirms it sounds fixed and doesn't push a repair, photos or a long chat.
Tells the tenant to report again if the screw keeps loosening or the hinge cracks, and logs a short low-priority note.

first: one of the floor tiles in the bathroom cracked, I took a pic if u want

tenant.situation: A floor tile in front of the bathtub has a crack across it. One corner piece moves a little when you step on it.

knows.where: bathroom floor, right in front of the tub
knows.appearance: one tile cracked corner to corner, a small piece rocks under your foot
knows.sharp: the edge isn't sharp, nothing is sticking up
knows.water: no water around it, the grout looks fine
knows.cause: you didn't drop anything that you remember
knows.tried: put the bath mat over it

doesnt_know: whether the floor underneath is damaged

truth.problem: Cracked floor tile, likely subfloor flex; replace the tile and check the subfloor.

judge: Takes the offered photo right away instead of asking for it later.
Asks whether water gets under it or the piece is loose, and mentions keeping water off the crack (bath mat, wipe up splashes).

first: carpet is wet by the patio door??

tenant.situation: The carpet in the living room right in front of the sliding patio door is soggy. It's been raining hard for two days.

knows.where: living room, the strip of carpet in front of the sliding patio door
knows.size: about a metre wide and 30 cm in
knows.since: noticed this morning, after two days of heavy rain
knows.water_track: you see water in the bottom track of the door, it looks full
knows.door: the door closes and locks fine

doesnt_know: whether the track weep holes are blocked
whether the door seal is bad

truth.problem: Blocked weep holes / failed sill seal on the sliding patio door letting rainwater over the track into the carpet.

judge: Asks whether it happens with rain and looks at the door track, linking the wet carpet to the patio door rather than a pipe.
Suggests safe steps like soaking up water, drying the carpet with a fan and clearing debris from the track.

first: le joint autour du bain est tout noir et ça décolle

tenant.situation: The white caulking where the bathtub meets the tiled wall is black with spots and peeling away at the corner.

knows.where: bathroom, along the back edge of the tub against the tiles
knows.appearance: black spots inside the caulk, a 20 cm piece peeling off in the corner by the taps
knows.since: getting worse for a few months
knows.water: you're not sure if water gets behind it; there's no stain on the ceiling below that you know of
knows.tried: scrubbed with a bathroom cleaner, it stays black

doesnt_know: whether water is getting into the wall
tenant.style: writes only in French, casual, short messages

truth.problem: Mouldy, failed silicone caulking at the tub-wall joint; needs to be removed and re-caulked before water gets behind the tile.

judge: Explains that peeling caulk can let water behind the wall and the manager should have it redone, while the tenant keeps the area dry after showers.
Does not suggest the tenant re-caulk or cut it out themselves as the fix.

first: 窗户漏风 晚上好冷

tenant.situation: Cold air comes in around the bedroom window even when it's closed and locked. The room is much colder than the rest of the unit.

knows.what: you feel cold air along the side where the two panes meet and at the bottom
knows.closed: it's closed and the latch is locked
knows.seal: the rubber strip on one side is loose and hanging
knows.since: you noticed when it got cold this week
knows.heat: the heater works, the room just loses heat
knows.tried: put a towel on the sill

doesnt_know: whether the weatherstripping can be replaced
tenant.style: writes only in simplified Chinese, short messages

truth.problem: Worn/detached weatherstripping on a sliding window.

judge: Checks that the window is fully closed and latched, then asks about the seal and records the loose weatherstripping.
Offers a safe stopgap (towel or draft stopper) and does not suggest taping over or blocking a heater.

first: paint in the bathroom is bubbling and peeling, also the fan doesnt really do anything

tenant.situation: The paint on the bathroom ceiling and the wall above the shower is bubbling and peeling. The bathroom fan hums but barely pulls air, and the mirror stays foggy a long time.

knows.where: bathroom ceiling over the shower and the top of the wall beside it
knows.appearance: bubbles and flakes of paint, some small grey spots
knows.fan: it makes noise but a tissue held up to it doesn't move
knows.shower: you shower daily, the room stays steamy for 30 minutes
knows.tried: leave the door open after showers

doesnt_know: whether the fan duct is blocked

truth.problem: Bathroom exhaust fan not venting (failed motor or blocked duct) causing moisture damage to the paint; fix fan, then scrape and repaint with bathroom paint.

judge: Handles both problems and links them: the weak fan is the likely cause of the peeling paint.
The ticket names both the fan and the paint damage so one visit can fix the cause first.
